source: Remote work always increases productivity because our team closed more tickets last month. Team size also increased last month.
expectations: Clarify productivity and challenge the causal universal.
Retain team-size change as an alternative explanation.
Offer a bounded statement supported by the observation.

source: Rewrite this recommendation after checking its assumptions; give me the finished paragraph. We should add a retry because a test request failed once; the failure cause is unknown.
expectations: Perform self-review and deliver a paragraph rather than an unsolicited interview.
Keep the unknown cause and avoid treating retries as proven effective.
knownBadRewrite: First answer ten questions before I write anything.

source: The survey suggests that some users prefer the new navigation; only 12 volunteers responded.
expectations: Preserve suggests, some, volunteer sampling, and n=12.
Do not claim a representative preference for all users.
Identify whom the survey observed before discussing the larger subscriber population.
request: Revise a claim that this survey generalizes to all subscribers, giving the strongest supported conclusion.

source: An accessibility office says all commuters will read the new sign faster. Volunteer cyclists familiar with the route read it in five seconds on average, two seconds faster than similar cyclists shown the old sign. A new lamp lit only the new sign. Recover the old timing and assess the claim.
expectations: Report five seconds versus seven for volunteer cyclists familiar with the route. Only the new sign was lit by the new lamp, so the sign change alone cannot explain the difference with certainty.
Extending the result to unfamiliar commuters or other conditions requires comparable effects; this test did not measure them.

source: In year one, customer wait times did not differ. In year two, clinics using a new scheduler recorded a three-minute shorter wait, but only those clinics also hired a nurse. A hospital predicts the same three-minute reduction. What does this evidence support?
expectations: Keep the first-year null separate from the second-year difference. The measurement does not isolate the scheduler from staffing or establish how a different hospital will respond.
